definition: An outlet's articles are shown only if it passes two tests, checked on 18 Nov 2026 with sources: (1) independent: no church, political party or government controls it, unless a law or charter guarantees its editorial independence (as for the BBC or Deutsche Welle); (2) its own reporting: a news agency, a broadcaster or newspaper with its own correspondents, a humanitarian specialist with field staff, or a local outlet with reporters where displacement happens. Each outlet records which outside databases list it (Journalism Trust Initiative, ReliefWeb sources, Reuters Institute Digital News Report, European Broadcasting Union, Public Media Alliance, The Trust Project, press councils). Local outlets whose owner is not published but show no sign of outside control are kept and marked 'owner not published'. UN and intergovernmental bodies count as official sources. Aggregators, press-release sites, tabloids and trade press are blocked; outlets that failed a test are listed under 'excluded' with the reason.

levels.checked: Owner published, or listed by an outside trust database
levels.owner-not-published: Owner not published or not confirmed; has its own reporters and no sign of government, party or church control

tiers.newspaper: Newspaper of record or major national outlet
tiers.humanitarian: Humanitarian or migration specialist, UN agency or NGO
tiers.regional: Regional or national outlet covering a region with few international reporters

intergovernmental.source: Any .int domain (IANA grants .int only to treaty-based intergovernmental bodies, https://www.iana.org/domains/int/policy), plus UN system organizations in the UN System Chief Executives Board directory (https://unsceb.org/directory)
